provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Salat: praying together
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state the importance of praying together.
The pupils should be able to identify the Imam during prayer.

Introduction:
We pray five times every day. We can pray alone or with others.

Content:
Salat is prayer. Muslims pray in the mosque. The Imam leads the prayer. We stand in straight rows. We follow the Imam's movements. We say "Allahu Akbar" together.

Class activity:
Let's practice standing in rows. One pupil will be the Imam and others will follow.

Evaluation questions:
What is Salat?
Who leads the prayer?
What do we say before we start praying?

Summary:
Praying together shows unity in Islam.

topics.title: The month of Ramadan
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain what fasting means.
The pupils should be able to list two benefits of fasting.

Introduction:
We eat three meals every day. Ramadan is a special month.

Content:
Ramadan is the ninth month of Islamic calendar. Muslims fast from sunrise to sunset. Fasting means no food or drink. We learn self-control. We feel for poor people. We break fast with dates.

Class activity:
Let's pretend to fast until the bell rings for break time.

Evaluation questions:
When do Muslims fast?
What do we eat to break fast?
Why do we fast?

Summary:
Ramadan teaches us patience and thankfulness.

topics.title: Giving to the poor
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to define Zakat.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate giving with a happy face.

Introduction:
Some people have little food. We can help them.

Content:
Zakat is giving to the poor. It is one of five pillars of Islam. We give money or food. Allah sees our giving. We should smile when we give. Helping makes us happy.

Class activity:
Let's give pretend coins to our friends with a big smile.

Evaluation questions:
What is Zakat?
Who do we give Zakat to?
How should we feel when we give?

Summary:
Giving to the poor shows we care for others.

topics.title: Surah Al-Ikhlas
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite Surah Al-Ikhlas.
The pupils should be able to explain that Allah is one.

Introduction:
The Qur'an has many small chapters. Surah Al-Ikhlas is one.

Content:
Surah Al-Ikhlas is chapter 112. It says Allah is one. Allah does not have children. Allah is the only one to worship. We recite it in prayer.

Class activity:
Let's recite Surah Al-Ikhlas together with actions.

Evaluation questions:
What number is Surah Al-Ikhlas?
What does Surah Al-Ikhlas teach us?
How many times do we recite it daily?

Summary:
Surah Al-Ikhlas reminds us Allah is one.

topics.title: Honesty in Islam
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify honesty as good behavior.
The pupils should be able to tell one story about a truthful child.

Introduction:
Sometimes we want to hide the truth. Islam teaches us to be honest.

Content:
Honesty means always telling the truth. Allah loves honest people. The Prophet Muhammad was always honest. When we lie, we make Allah sad. Truthful people have good character.

Class activity:
Let's play a game where we practice telling the truth.

Evaluation questions:
What is honesty?
What does Allah like?
Can you tell a story about a truthful child?

Summary:
Honesty is very important in Islam.

topics.title: Obedience to parents
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state why we should obey parents.
The pupils should be able to list two ways to show obedience.

Introduction:
Our parents take care of us every day. We must listen to them.

Content:
Allah loves children who obey their parents. We must say "yes ma" and "yes sir". We must help our parents. We must not shout at them. Obedience brings blessings from Allah.

Class activity:
Let's practice saying "yes ma" and "yes sir" to the teacher.

Evaluation questions:
What does Allah like?
How should we talk to our parents?
Why must we obey our parents?

Summary:
Obeying parents is pleasing to Allah.

topics.title: Cleanliness in Islam
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain that cleanliness is part of faith.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate clean habits.

Introduction:
We wash our hands before eating. Cleanliness is important in Islam.

Content:
Cleanliness is part of faith. We must be clean every day. We wash our hands, face and body. We keep our homes clean. We wear clean clothes. Clean places make us happy.

Class activity:
Let's practice washing our hands the right way.

Evaluation questions:
What is cleanliness?
When should we wash our hands?
Why is cleanliness important?

Summary:
Islam teaches us to be clean always.

topics.title: My name in Islam
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state their own name.
The pupils should be able to identify good Islamic names.

Introduction:
Every child has a name. Some names have special meanings.

Content:
Muslims have good names. Names like Aisha, Ibrahim and Fatima are good. Your name was chosen with love. Some names mean "servant of Allah". We should be proud of our names.

Class activity:
Let's say our names and what they mean.

Evaluation questions:
What is your name?
What makes a name good?
Can you name two good Muslim names?

Summary:
Our names show who we are in Islam.

topics.title: Love for the Qur'an
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite a short verse from the Qur'an.
The pupils should be able to explain how to care for the Qur'an.

Introduction:
The Qur'an is Allah's book. We must love and respect it.

Content:
The Qur'an has Allah's words. We must listen when it is recited. We must keep the Qur'an clean. We must not put it on the floor. We should read it every day.

Class activity:
Let's practice holding the Qur'an with two hands carefully.

Evaluation questions:
What is the Qur'an?
How should we treat the Qur'an?
Why do we love the Qur'an?

Summary:
The Qur'an is a precious gift from Allah.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to answer questions about term's work.
The pupils should be able to recite Surah Al-Ikhlas.

Introduction:
Today we will remember what we learned this term.

Content:
We learned about Salat, Ramadan, Zakat, Surah Al-Ikhlas, honesty, obedience, cleanliness, names and the Qur'an. All these are important in Islam.

Class activity:
Let's play a quiz about what we learned this term.

Evaluation questions:
What are the five pillars of Islam?
Why do we fast in Ramadan?
How should we treat our parents?

Summary:
Let's remember these lessons for our whole life.
